title: Humanity's Last Exam
hook: Humanity's Last Exam is a 3,000-question expert benchmark built to be the hardest closed-ended test there is — designed to outlast frontier models as MMLU saturated.
key_points: Released January 2025 by the Center for AI Safety (CAIS) and Scale AI.
3,000 expert-written questions (2,500 public) spanning 100+ academic disciplines.
Built to combat saturation after top models exceeded 90% on tests like MMLU.
At launch, leading models answered well under 10% correctly.
content_html: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE), released in January 2025 by the Center for AI Safety and Scale AI, is a benchmark deliberately built to be the hardest closed-ended academic test of its kind. It collects 3,000 expert-level questions across more than a hundred disciplines — math, the sciences, the humanities — written and vetted by specialists, with a private subset held back to detect overfitting.
extra_html:
How it works

The motivation was benchmark saturation: by early 2025, frontier models were scoring above 90% on established tests like MMLU, so those tests no longer separated the best systems. HLE's creators crowdsourced and filtered tens of thousands of candidate questions — offering prizes for the best — down to a final set hard enough that, at launch, leading models answered fewer than 10% correctly. The benchmark is multi-modal and spans expert frontiers of human knowledge.

Why it matters

A useful benchmark has to be hard enough to leave headroom; once models ace it, it stops measuring progress. HLE was an attempt to build a test that would stay meaningful as capabilities climbed — its very name a wry bet that it might be among the last purely academic exams models can't trivially pass. Tracking movement on HLE became a way to gauge genuine expert-level reasoning rather than recall.

related.title: MMLU: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
related.hook: Want one number for how broadly an LLM 'knows stuff'? MMLU is a 57-subject exam spanning history, law, medicine, and math — and it became a default yardstick.

related.title: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark
related.hook: What makes a question hard for a model? GPQA's are hard even for skilled people with Google: non-experts reach only 34% after 30+ minutes of searching.

related.title: On the Measure of Intelligence (ARC)
related.hook: Is a high benchmark score the same as intelligence? Chollet argues no — intelligence is how efficiently you acquire new skills, not how well you perform known ones.

related.title: Agents' Last Exam: Benchmarking Agents on Real Economic Work
related.hook: Frontier agents ace academic benchmarks but flop on real jobs — Agents' Last Exam scores them on 1,000+ economically valuable workflows, where the hardest tier sees just a 2.6% pass rate.
